lots.what_it_is: LAG Tramontane auditorium cutaway acoustic-electric guitar in a brown sunburst (LAG call it Brown Shadow, BRS) finish, with a floor stand. Gowans title: LAG TRAMONTANE T100ACE ACOUSTIC/ELECTRIC GUITAR WITH STAND. Most likely a T100ACE-BRS, which Reverb lists as a real factory variant.
lots.score_reason: Overseas used asking prices for T100ACE variants run about AUD 500 to 680, and a new T100ACE-BRS is listed from about AUD 638. Realistic Australian used value is probably AUD 300 to 450. I knocked it down because there are no sold prices, the model label is not readable in the photo and the electronics have not been checked.
lots.key_photo_findings: One photo only. Headstock has the LAG logo and a dark wood face. There is an Occitan cross inlay below the soundhole, a wooden rosette, a winged bridge with a pin row, a wedge-shaped end inlay at the tail, binding, and a single Venetian-style cutaway. Brown sunburst on a cedar-coloured top. All of this matches the Tramontane line and Reverb's stock photo of the T100ACE-BRS (Brown Sunburst). This also settles the researcher's worry that a sunburst top can't be a T100ACE. A label is visible inside the soundhole but too small to read. The preamp side panel is out of view, so the electronics (StudioLag) are unconfirmed. No obvious cracks or big dings on the top at this resolution. Gowans list it with a stand, no case.
lots.condition: Looks clean and complete from the front, with strings on and no visible top damage at photo resolution. Back, sides, neck, frets, electronics and battery are not seen or tested.

lots.what_it_is: Single live-edge timber slab, catalogued by Gowans as Huon pine. Pale straw colour, knotty, with burl-like areas toward the top. Length roughly 2m, width estimated at about 250 to 400mm (wider at the top), thickness unknown.
lots.score_reason: If it is genuine Huon pine, dealer prices for plain or flawed slabs of similar size run AUD 205 to 490, and an auction slab of unknown thickness and grade will usually make well under retail. The species is the seller's claim only, and I found no sold evidence.
lots.key_photo_findings: One photo. The slab stands against a wall, chalked 1315 and 2/10/26, with a Gowans sticker. It is pale cream to light yellow with a fine, even grain, scattered small dark knots, and a lumpy figured area at the top right with a dark knot or void. Both edges are natural live edge, waisted near the base, with a small split or rough end at the bottom. It looks sawn and not dressed. Thickness can't be seen. Huon pine is plausible from the colour and small knots, but celery top pine, King Billy or macrocarpa can't be ruled out from a photo, so it needs a smell and close look at the preview.
lots.condition: Rough sawn, appears sound with no obvious rot, with knots and a likely small end check at the bottom. Thickness and moisture are unknown.
